newsitem.title: USA: CME fines bank, broker $200,000 for rules breach.
newsitem.headline: CME fines bank, broker $200,000 for rules breach.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said Friday it fined a bank futures unit and a floor broker a total of $200,000 for breaking rules regarding handling of customer orders and record-keeping in 1995 and 1996.
The CME said it fined Citicorp Futures Corp $50,000 and member John M Murphy $150,000, under offers of settlement effective today. CME also suspended Murphy for 75 days.

Citicorp and Murphy neither admitted nor denied July 30 findings of a CME agricultural committee that alleged that at times in 1995 and 1996 they guaranteed prices and quantities for customer orders and failed to keep proper trade records.
The CME also alleged that Murphy compelled order adjustments from floor brokers, improperly refused futures fills and aided in preparation of inaccurate order tickets.
